newsitem.title: HONDURAS: HONDURAS SETS UP EMERGENCY EL NINO PLAN FOR CROPS.
newsitem.headline: HONDURAS SETS UP EMERGENCY EL NINO PLAN FOR CROPS.

text.p: Honduras announced Wednesday an emergency farm plan for a region in the south of the country that has been deprived of rains because of the impact of "El Nino", officials said.

Food will be handed out in exchange for work according to the plan worked out by President Carlos Reina's agricultural cabinet after meetings with cattlemen and farm leaders from the Choluteca region.

Agriculture and Livestock Minister Ricardo Arias told reporters that El Nino has caused rains to be delayed in the region and had brought important crop losses for corn, beans and sorghum crops in the Choluteca and Valle regions and the zones around Francisco Morazan, El Paraiso and La Paz.
Part of the plan is also to drill wells to reach subsurface water, construct irrigation systems and build temporary reservoirs, he added.
Grains will be distributed in local stores and businesses, and farmers will be encouraged to diversify crops.
Local authorities claim that 95 percent of crops in the region have been lost. No figures were available to indicate specific crop volumes in the region.
El Nino is a weather pattern that warms waters off the South American Pacific coasts and can have a profound impact on global patterns for as long as 18 months.
